text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: canary pool 'canary-eu-1' exhibiting sustained p99 latency > 1.8s after deploy (deploy-bot: deploy/2026-03-15/rls-617). Auto-escalation triggered. :rotating_light:

sara: ack - oncall here, pulling logs. which rollout is this?

deploy-bot: roll: rls-617 -> feature: continuous-batching-v2 enabled on 25% canary.

mike: I pushed the batching kernel change in rls-617. Not seeing errors in smoke, but canary telemetry shows kernel fallback on a subset of GPU nodes.

leo: summary from metrics: throughput drop ~30% for the canary slice, p95->p99 gap growing, error rate small but timeouts at 10s increased. Some nodes reported kernel mismatch and fell back to cpu exec path.

sara: ok standing up quick checklist: 1) stop canary traffic, 2) flip kill-switch for continuous-batching-v2, 3) if perf doesn't recover, start rollback. Triage owners: @mike kernel/batching, @leo routing/traffic, @tara escalation/CS.

mike: trying to flip the kill-switch now: `rbac feature flip continuous-batching-v2=false --env canary-eu-1`

mike: returned 200, feature flag off for canary-eu-1.

sara: thanks. leo, can you reassign traffic away from affected slice?

leo: routing change in progress: `routectl set-slice-weight canary-eu-1 0.0 --gradual 30s`

incident-bot: routing event recorded.

cs-rep: FYI: we have two customers (acct: spinrise, acct: wordly-ai) who reported slow responses in the last 15m. CS has opened a preliminary incident ticket and I informed them we are triaging.

mike: look at node logs, sample: ```
E 15:22:08 kernel_select.cpp:142 kernel mismatch detected for model-xyz -> fallback to cpu_kernel (reason: unsupported_conv_winograd)
W 15:22:09 batching_scheduler.cpp:88 batch size drop from 48->8 due to slot starvation
```

mike: appears batching heuristics + new kernel selection policy caused uneven sloting on some hosts; that triggered fallback which then ballooned cpu path latency.

tara: can we confirm scope of customer impact? CS, any confirmed errors or degraded SLAs?

cs-rep: CS notes: 12 support pings in last 20m, 3 timeouts logged, majority saw 2-3x latency. No major uptime failures yet. Customers flagged for follow-up.

sara: good. mitigation timeline: 00:00 - flip flag (done), 00:45 - route off (in progress), 01:20 - if metrics not back to baseline, rollback. Right now monitor for 5m.

leo: routing completed. canary-eu-1 slice weight -> 0. Traffic drained.

mike: after flag flip and drain, p95 improved ~30%, p99 still slightly elevated but trending down. No new kernel fallback messages in last 3m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD#INC-8283 -> acknowledged by sara.

sara: given improvement, we won't full rollback yet. plan: abort staged rollout (stop further canaries), schedule rollback for tomorrow controlled window if regression reappears, and open a hotfix PR to adjust kernel selection heuristics.

mike: creating PR now: `pr create --title "fix: kernel selection edge-case for conv_winograd" --base main`

mike: PR 8792 opened. adding perf tests.

tara: I'll prep a short customer update for CS and add to incident slack channel. CS: please send a note to affected accounts saying we mitigated and are investigating root cause.

cs-rep: will do, drafting now.

sara: handing off to day oncall @leo for next 6 hours for follow-up and postmortem. If regressions spike again, escalate to oncall rotation immediately.

leo: ack taking over. I'll monitor for 2h and coordinate with eng-runtime for a targeted rollback if needed.

mike: tagging telemetry dashboard and logs for postmortem: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/canary-latency?orgId=1&var-rollout=rls-617

sara: adding this thread to incident tracker and creating initial postmortem stub. log all actions + timestamps there.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation steps applied, customer impact limited, issue contained to canary slice. Next update in 60m or sooner on regression. :white_check_mark:
